metadata.title: Checking a Pitch Deck Before It Goes Out.
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: what does it actually mean to have Claude check a pitch deck before it goes out? Lands the carry-out that a skill like this reconciles a deck (the same four checks, every slide, every run) rather than proofreading it.
metadata.anchor_pair: N/A — source is skill-teardown format (anatomy -> pipeline -> constraint -> verdict), no anchor structure to preserve

beats.narration_text: Someone assumes checking a deck before sending it just means running a spellcheck. It doesn't. The real risk is numbers that stop matching across slides. Here's what an actual check catches.

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'Can Claude spellcheck my pitch deck before I send it?', hesitates on 'spellcheck', corrects to 'check'

beats.act: 1 anatomy — a skill is a folder
beats.narration_text: This kind of check is built from something called a skill — a folder Claude reads before it works. Inside is one file, written in plain language, that spells out exactly what to look for. Claude reads the file, then follows it. The file is the whole program.

shot.new_visual_element: A folder icon opening to reveal SKILL.md, references/, scripts/; SKILL.md highlighted

production_viz.label: A skill is a folder
production_viz.mechanic: A folder opens on cream to reveal three items: SKILL.md (highlighted in crimson), a references/ folder, a scripts/ folder. An arrow from SKILL.md loops to a small 'Claude reads, then follows it' caption.

beats.narration_text: The steps run in order: read the file, work through each step exactly as written, then return the result. Nothing runs out of sequence unless a step itself says so.

shot.new_visual_element: Three-phase pipeline: Read SKILL.md -> Execute steps in order -> Return result

production_viz.label: Input in, output out
production_viz.mechanic: Three cards left to right joined by arrows: 'Read SKILL.md', 'Execute steps in order', 'Return result'. Linear, no branch points drawn.

beats.narration_text: For this skill, the checklist itself is four things: do the numbers agree across every slide, does the story match the underlying data, does the language hold up against IB standards, and is the formatting clean. Run it on the same deck twice and it flags the same four things — nothing outside that list gets checked.

shot.new_visual_element: Four checklist items with checkmarks: numbers agree, story matches data, language holds up, formatting is clean; a boundary line with 'nothing outside this list' beyond it

production_viz.label: Exactly four checks
production_viz.mechanic: Four checklist rows fill in one at a time with a checkmark: 'Numbers agree across slides', 'Story matches the data', 'Language holds up (IB standard)', 'Formatting is clean'. A dashed boundary line beneath the list, with a faint unlabelled field beyond it captioned 'nothing outside this list'.

beats.narration_text: A skill like this doesn't proofread a deck — it reconciles it: the same four checks, every slide, every run, and nothing outside that checklist gets caught.

props.quote: A skill like this doesn't proofread a deck — it reconciles it: the same four checks, every slide, every run, and nothing outside that checklist gets caught.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. Ask Claude: check this pitch deck for four things — numbers that don't match across slides, claims that don't match the underlying data, language that doesn't fit the audience it's going to, and any formatting that's inconsistent. List exactly what to fix before it goes out. Liam, in for Bear.
